title: Fix SOME/IP Protocol Packet Dissection in Wireshark
description:
Starting Wireshark and attempting to directly dissect a SOME/IP protocol packets leads to the dissector failing to parse the base types. This bug arises from the initialization of more complex types before the base types from the configuration file.
This merge request addresses the issue by reordering the initialization process in the config file to ensure that base types are initialized before more complex types. This adjustment allows for correct parsing of base types in Wireshark.

Verified the fix by testing with various SOME/IP protocol packets to ensure accurate dissection in Wireshark.

Yes, I will.

Is there a trace and config that shows the issues?

If the order of the UAT definitions would play a role into a bug behavior, I do not think that reordering them could work as they can reference each other.

My trace file is this [trace.pcap](/uploads/864ab24f48d2da774a08ee2ba0c927bd/trace.pcap), using the config files:
[SOMEIP_parameter_structs](/uploads/d2aa36573cc0e9a69d2a4b85cc2edadc/SOMEIP_parameter_structs)
[SOMEIP_parameter_arrays](/uploads/4450e99a00d3ff11f89df5e784af0c08/SOMEIP_parameter_arrays)
[SOMEIP_parameter_base_types](/uploads/c666e2d8aa573fff3242f69790b2537d/SOMEIP_parameter_base_types)
[SOMEIP_parameter_enums](/uploads/f7da42fbf91b8aaf35fd9b912f1d41d7/SOMEIP_parameter_enums)
[SOMEIP_parameter_list](/uploads/99877b4e8f2b7c4eedcac148e00c2ede/SOMEIP_parameter_list)

Unfortunately, my fix is viable for my specific case where I have a struct that contains base types.

The issue is that get_param_attributes() that is called by post_update_someip_leap_parameter_struct_cb(), calls get_enum_config() which looks inside data_someip_leap_parameter_enums which is NULL because post_update_someip_leap_parameter_enum_cb() has not ran yet.

A runtime fix for this would be to re-trigger the "Dissect Payload" option which will rerun post_update_someip_leap_parameter_struct_cb(), but this time data_someip_leap_parameter_enums has content from the first initialization. 

In the case where types would reference each other (stuct inside a struct), the bug would most certainly persist.

Which version of Wireshark are you using and what is the behavior of the bug?

With a 4.2.3. it seems to be ok!?
![image](/uploads/5677b42502387bcd461b32cc9b435a3e/image.png)

P.S. What is post_update_someip_leap_parameter_struct_cb ? Is the "leap" a mistake?
P.S. Setting the filter string for every element to 0 is not a great idea, as this would mean that Wireshark generates always the same filter. You need to make sure that these are unique!

I was using 4.2.2 and updated to 4.2.3, I even tried a fresh install on another PC and it still doesn't seem to work for me.
![image](/uploads/46cb5c1b8469a07f2c204d098246fcef/image.png)
Did you do some additional steps? Tweaking parameters or anything else that affects the configuration makes it work.

I haven't given much thought about the filter string, I will look into it.
As for the "leap" string, yes it's a mistake, I copied it from a custom plugin.

I just:
- created an empty profile directory
- copied your files in
- opened the trace
- clicked on the single packet and selected decode as SOME/IP

Do you maybe have some Lua scripts installed that interfere?

I used macOS for test, what are you using?

Since I tried on a fresh install on Windows OS, no plugins were present. My steps were:
- copy files inside the profile directory
- open trace
- check someip_tcp_heur and someip_udp_heur \
![image](/uploads/0ff403aea17bf55066f4f486dddd39d0/image.png)
- click on the packet

I tried your way, by setting the decoding as SOME/IP instead of using the heuristic dissectors and it works!
Perhaps the intended way of use is the decode config, not the heuristic dissector.

I finally could reproduce it. I needed to take out the port number, activate heuristics, exit Wireshark, start Wireshark and I see the issue.

I will look into this but I am very sure that the this MR will not solve the issue as reordering cannot work due to cyclic dependencies.

Can you please raise an issue with the information from here attached but close this MR?

Sure, I will.
Thanks for helping out.
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/19670
